title: CloudFront Origin Security & Private Content
summary: Lock origins behind CloudFront and serve private content with signed URLs, cookies and OAC.
tldr: S3 behind CloudFront: keep the bucket **private**, use **origin access control (OAC)**, and allow only that distribution in the bucket policy. OAC replaces the legacy OAI and supports SSE-KMS.
ALB or EC2 that must not be internet-facing: use **CloudFront VPC origins** with an internal ALB in private subnets.
Paid or private content: **signed URLs** for one file, **signed cookies** for many files (HLS segments, a whole course). Upload/download directly to S3 from a browser: **S3 presigned URL**.

keyFacts.text: Signed URLs and cookies are verified with public keys in a **trusted key group**; use key groups, not the legacy root-user CloudFront key pairs.
CloudFront **field-level encryption** encrypts chosen POST form fields at the edge with your public key, so only the holder of the private key can read them downstream.
Allow or block lists by country at the distribution level; blocked viewers get HTTP 403.
An ACM certificate used by CloudFront must be requested in **us-east-1**, whatever Region the origin is in.

keywords.cue: S3 bucket accessible only through CloudFront
keywords.answer: Origin access control (OAC) with bucket policy

keywords.cue: ALB must not be internet-facing behind CloudFront
keywords.answer: Internal ALB as a CloudFront VPC origin

keywords.cue: hundreds of HLS segments for paying users
keywords.answer: CloudFront signed cookies with a trusted key group

keywords.cue: browser uploads large files directly to a private bucket
keywords.answer: S3 presigned PUT URL from the backend

keywords.cue: encrypt one sensitive form field end to end
block viewers from specific countries with 403

traps: **OAI** is legacy; new answers use **OAC**, which also works with SSE-KMS encrypted objects.
Signed URLs for hundreds of segment files are impractical; signed cookies cover them all.
A presigned URL is S3's feature, not CloudFront's; it bypasses CloudFront caching.
Restricting an ALB security group to CloudFront IPs still leaves the ALB public; VPC origins remove that exposure.
